Case Study: A Surveyor's Drone Climb

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

A land-survey team launches a mapping drone that rises in a perfectly straight line from its launch pad at A(2,3,1) to a hover point B(5,7,13), all coordinates in metres on the site grid (with x east, y north and z vertical). The pilot needs the drone's heading described both as a set of direction ratios and as direction cosines, because the flight-control software stores a bearing as a unit direction. Knowing the exact climb also lets the team check the length of a tethered power cable running along the same path. They treat the pad and the hover point as two fixed points in space, read off the displacement between them, and reduce it to the three cosines of the angles the path makes with the east, north and vertical axes before uploading the route.
